subject: Theme library research: adopt VS Code color-theme JSON as the import standard; convert into the existing --oi-* role tokens
result: RESEARCH ONLY (no code changed). Commission: how to give the desktop a host of themes under a standard like VS Code's. FINDING: the app already has the hard part. packages/oi-design-system/tokens.css is a role-token system (consumers use var(--oi-*) only; role names never change; hosts theme by overriding tokens), with a light appearance block and a dark block selected by .oi-desktop[data-theme] before first paint. Every consuming surface is already var-driven: CodeMirror highlight style reads var(--oi-syntax-*) (desktop/cradle/src/editor/TextEditor.tsx:52-62), the terminal reads the same variables and re-reads when data-theme flips (src/terminal/TerminalSurface.tsx), native theme sync exists (src/workspace/nativeTheme.ts). A theme is therefore a value-set for the existing roles; the missing pieces are a theme format, a loader, and a library. RECOMMENDED SHAPE: (1) treat VS Code color-theme JSON as the authoring/import standard, not the app-native format: it is JSON(C) with name, type (dark/light/hcBlack/hcLight), include (inheritance), colors (400+ workbench UI keys), tokenColors (TextMate scope rules), semanticTokenColors; official JSON schema published (schemastore vscode-color-theme.json; source microsoft/vscode src/vs/workbench/services/themes/common/color-theme-schema.ts); filename convention *.color-theme.json gives free editor validation. (2) A build-time converter maps a VS Code theme onto the --oi-* roles into a normalized oi.theme document; unknown VS Code keys are ignored, unmappable keys drop. The design-law tension is real and belongs in the mapping table's custody: the house language keeps accent-as-ink and scarce gold, so imported themes color the roles, never add chrome roles or change role names. (3) TextMate scopes need one bounded scope-suffix table (~30 rules) onto the 13 existing --oi-syntax-* roles (keyword/string/comment/literal/type/definition/...); the roles currently all collapse to foreground/muted in house themes but can carry distinct colors, so imported themes render faithfully with zero editor changes. CodeMirror 6 does not consume TextMate scopes natively (known ecosystem friction; common routes are hand-mapping or via Shiki) — our roles sidestep it. (4) Terminal maps directly: VS Code terminal.ansiBlack..BrightWhite, terminal.background/foreground/selectionBackground -> xterm ITheme (background/foreground/selectionBackground/black..brightWhite). (5) Library supply: bundle converted copies of MIT-licensed popular themes (Dracula, Nord, Tokyo Night, One Dark Pro, Catppuccin, GitHub Light/Dark, Night Owl; check each license before bundling); monaco-themes npm 0.4.8 carries 56 ready TextMate-derived JSON themes (verified by downloading the package) runnable through the same converter; Tinted Theming Base16/24 (200+ YAML schemes) and themer/themer.dev are generation standards if the owner wants themes authored in the house language instead of ports; an import-from-disk picker (accept any .json theme; optionally read ~/.vscode/extensions/*/themes/*.json) reaches the whole marketplace without bundling. (6) Settings surface: extend Visuals -> Themes from the light/dark/system pair to named themes via the same data-theme attribute + MutationObserver + before-first-paint mechanism, with previews rendered from the normalized doc. Follow-up agent: this record is the plan source; read it plus tokens.css, DESKTOP-LANGUAGE.md, and TextEditor.tsx, then propose the mapping table and converter as the first increment.
